I think The Dark Knight was special because it changed how people approached the particular genre of movies. Its the "gold standard".
Do The Right Thing. Awful movie. Totally glorified characters for acting like spoiled, entitled children.

Blue is the Warmest Color. It's really well made, but I felt the relationships and the characters were hollow. The sex scenes were the most ridiculous I have ever seen. Everyone was appalled by them, including the author of the original comic book.

Read the comic book instead. It's a flawed, but way better display of love.
Gone Girl. It was at best ok. But I read the book first, so that didn't help.
Yes, given the star power behind it it was quite disappointing. The biggest surprise to me though was how badly cast NPH was, or else he's just not a very capable actor.

The Star Trek reboots. Such lifeless, uninteresting, and lazy films. B actors given mediocre dialogue in a series of contrived, CGI heavy set pieces. Not a speck of the mystique that made the series interesting in the first place was captured, other than the trotting out of cliches.

Full disclosure I have not actually stayed awake through either film, despite repeated attempts to view.

On a related note I do not have high expectations for The Force Awakens, but a boy can hope.

Gravity has a 98% critic rating on rotten tomatoes, I really don't see how it could earn that high of praise, I get the effects were great but I found the story-line extremely lacking and quite boring at times.
I couldn't agree more. I thought the "message" was overwhelmingly preachy, too.

I think Crash was one of the worst movies to ever get an Academy Award. It was like a collection of short stories tied together with the flimsiest of plot devices with all the subtlety and nuance of a sledgehammer. Very few movies make me angry about how bad they are halfway through, but Crash was one of them for me.

Honorable mentions: Hurt Locker and Zero Dark Thirty. Hurt Locker because of how ridiculously unrealistic the plot was. Zero Dark Thirty because there was only one character with any depth and she was really bitchy and they made it seem like she was the only one working to bring down bin Laden. Oh, and the whole gratuitous torture thing.

I absolutely hated "The Hangover". I watched it twice and I still couldn't understand why people thought it was so hilarious. I kind of chuckled at some parts, but it wasn't over the top laughter like the majority of the audience. Also, I think people constantly quoting the movie in everyday life made it worse for me.

I watched the Godfather movies, and while they were enjoyable, I can't help but feel that they are massively overrated. It isn't that they're slow, because I thought they were paced well, but I just didn't find them nearly as enjoyable as everyone makes them out to be. I couldn't help think "yes, but why?" whenever they go over the characters' motivations for what they do. Is it money? Why do they want this money? It's family, but most of the family members have really tenuous connections within the family, and the closest ones get killed off, often by their closest family members. Is it fame? Nope, they're criminals, and it isn't like they're trying to stick it to someone. I just thought they were exhausting, with very little payoff.

The Good, The Bad and The Ugly was The Boring. I wanted to get through it because I wanted to see what the fuss was all about, but it's way too simplistic to warrant the massive amount of praise that it gets.
Big 6 terrible movie. If the professor didn't kill his brother he would have never gotten his daughter back. The bad guy wins in the end even though he is arrested he wins in the end.
The vast majority of military movies are overrated in my opinion. I feel like if you make an overly "Murican'" movie it will always do well because people feel they have to like it.

Guardians of the Galaxy. I generally enjoy superhero movies, but this was a total turd IMO. Cheesy, cliche, god-mode = on, average Joe superhero.
